Jev-Urdu is Muhammad Noman's Urdu-first decision model with a multilingual mmBERT-base encoder and a decision head. Reported evaluation covers independent Urdu and Roman Urdu benchmarks, with mixed Urdu-English evaluated in a narrow internal workflow harness. English prompts change question and option language, not passage language. Full-suite results, matched API samples, batch throughput, and calibration limitations are documented separately in the launch article. Further-language performance is not established by this release. The jev-urdu 0.1.0 Python library is published on PyPI at https://pypi.org/project/jev-urdu/0.1.0/ (Python 3.10+); install with python -m pip install jev-urdu==0.1.0, import jev_urdu, then call jev_urdu.load(). Library documentation: https://huggingface.co/muhammadnoman76/jev-urdu/blob/main/library/README.md. The library downloads and caches the separately published model when loaded.

PawSip is Muhammad Noman's free Windows water-reminder app with an animated vector cat companion and desktop widget. Reminders follow the user's presence (screen on, unlocked, recent keyboard or mouse input), wait during fullscreen apps, and repeat every 15 minutes until a drink is logged. Version 1.0.2 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). Data stays on the PC. From 1.0.2 it updates itself: about 30 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads the JSON feed at https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/pawsip.json (an ordinary HTTPS request; nothing else is sent), offers a newer version on its dashboard or with a tray notification that waits while a fullscreen app runs, and on Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256, installs it silently for the current user and starts again in the tray. The check can be turned off in Settings › Updates. Resource figures in the article were measured on the author's Windows 11 PC; the ARM64 and Windows 7 builds were not tested on their native hardware.

VibePlayer is Muhammad Noman's free Windows media player with a YouTube-style interface, written in C# with WPF on LibVLC 3.0.24 (the engine inside VLC media player, used under the LGPL; VibePlayer is not affiliated with VideoLAN). Its skip mode lets the user mark parts of a video, by typing start and end times or pressing [ and ] while watching; the player jumps over those parts every time that file plays, checking the position every 40 ms. Marks are stored per file in the app's settings (%APPDATA%\VibePlayer) and the video file is never modified; skips apply to local files, not network streams. It opens 47 video and 34 audio file types. Version 1.0.2 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). From 1.0.2 it updates itself: shortly after start-up and at most once a day it reads the JSON feed at https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/vibeplayer.json (an ordinary HTTPS request; nothing else is sent), offers a newer version in a non-modal card, and on Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256, installs it silently in place and restarts. The check can be turned off in Settings › Updates. The VibePlayer images and launch video on this site are recreations of the app's interface composited with Big Buck Bunny footage (© 2008 Blender Foundation, CC BY 3.0), not screenshots. The ARM64 build was not run on ARM hardware, and no build was run on an actual Windows 7 or 8.1 machine.

Trove is Muhammad Noman's free archive manager for Windows, written in C# with WPF on the official, unmodified 7z.dll from 7-Zip 26.04 (used under the GNU LGPL with the unRAR licence restriction; Trove is not affiliated with 7-Zip, Igor Pavlov or RARLAB), through its own COM interop. It has a Windows 11 (Fluent) look that follows light/dark mode and the accent colour. It opens ZIP, 7Z, RAR and RAR5 (including encrypted and multi-part), TAR, GZ, BZ2, XZ, ZST, ISO, CAB, WIM, DMG and many other formats the 7-Zip engine reads, plus split (.001) and self-extracting archives. It creates ZIP, 7Z, TAR, TAR.GZ and TAR.XZ, never RAR (the format is proprietary and the unRAR licence forbids it), with Store/Fastest/Balanced/Smallest levels (7-Zip levels 0/1/5/9), AES-256 passwords for ZIP and 7Z, hidden file names for 7Z, and split parts. Extraction blocks zip-slip entries (.., absolute paths, drive letters, paths through junctions), never creates links or alternate data streams, writes each file to a temporary part until 7-Zip reports it OK, never overwrites silently, and copies the Mark of the Web from downloaded archives. Setup can add a Trove submenu to File Explorer's right-click menu (on Windows 11 under "Show more options"). Version 1.0.0 has four installers: Windows 10/11 x64, ARM64 and 32-bit (self-contained .NET 10) and Windows 7 SP1/8.1 (.NET Framework 4.8). It updates itself: about 10 seconds after start-up and at most once a day it reads https://www.nomanshafiq.com/updates/trove.json (nothing else is sent), and Update now downloads the installer for its edition, verifies its size and SHA-256 and installs it silently. 85 engine tests pass on .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8. The still images of Trove on this site are real screenshots with demo files; the 74-second launch video on the article (English captions) recreates Trove’s interface from its source. The ARM64 build was not run on ARM hardware, no build was run on an actual Windows 7 or 8.1 machine, and the all-users installation was not tested.
